name: zzAJ1_pose

tests.name: the Dog publishes its canonical worn pose
every costume skin produced a costume attached to the Dog

detail.note: Relay OG is the canonical body and wears no costume, so four of five is the right answer. The costume is matched on its attachment parent, because the AI Companions are the same class and a class match picks one of them.

tests.name: the Dog's own pose changes between samples

detail.note: a pose that never moves compares equal to anything, so this is the positive control: if the canonical stack is not running, every clause below would pass on two frozen structs.

tests.name: every costume reports that its gait is driven from outside

detail.note: the flag says the costume has handed its gait to the canonical stack. A costume computing its own gait is the item 3 defect in its plainest form, whatever the numbers then agree on.

tests.name: every costume wears the pose the Dog published, field for field

detail.note: the founder's 'one canonical Relay Dog behavior stack; skins are cosmetic' as an exact question. This does not say the canonical pose LOOKS right, which is theirs to judge, and it does not cover walk, run, stop, turns, jump, fall or landing as performances.
